race_context: The district: Shelbyville Central Schools (SCS) serves the City of Shelbyville area in Shelby County {dlgf_scs}{at_jun26_24}. Its schools include Shelbyville High School, Shelbyville Middle School and elementary schools including Loper, Coulston and Thomas A. Hendricks {at_may20_26}{at_aug15_26}. Superintendent Dr. Matt Vance said in August 2025 that enrollment was declining; he was then in his fourth year leading the district {at_aug17_25}. The district reinstated a virtual program that had 22 students in December 2025, 12 of them new to the district {at_dec17_25}.

The board has seven members. In January 2026 they were Andrea Lee, Dr. Julie Ruschhaupt, Dr. James Rees, Michael Turner, Dennis Hearne, Amanda Bunton and Dr. Kate Garringer {at_jan26}. Seats are tied to residence districts; 2024 filings listed District 1 (Marion Township), District 3 (Addison Township) and District 4B (Addison Township, city) {at_jun26_24}. District 4 (precincts 1-20, 29 and 36) elected two members in 2022, from five candidates including David M. Finkel and James Rees {at_aug30_22}{at_nov22_results}. In 2024 Dennis Hearne won District 3 over Curt Johnson, 3,785 to 3,331; in District 4, Andrea L. Lee received 4,297 votes, Michael Turner 4,247 and Edward J. Small Jr. 1,777, and both Lee and Turner sit on the board {at_nov6_24}{at_jan26}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: District 2 and District 4 {in_list}. Amanda (Mandy) Bunton, a current board member, is the only District 2 candidate {in_list}{at_jan26}{at_may18_26}. In District 4, Dr. Julie Ruschhaupt was appointed by the board on June 26, 2025 to fill a vacant seat for the rest of the term, after the board took applications {at_jun13_25}{at_jun27_25}. Dr. James Rees, who ran in District 4 in 2022, is not on the 2026 list {at_aug30_22}{in_list}.

Seat count in District 4 is uncertain: the state list says 'vote for 1', but District 4 elected two members in 2022 and two in 2024, and the 2026 seats appear to be the two filled in 2022 (the appointed Ruschhaupt seat and the Rees seat) {in_list}{at_aug30_22}{at_nov6_24}{at_jan26}. If two District 4 seats are on the ballot, both candidates, Ruschhaupt and Sara DePrez Lewis, would be elected. This guide did not find a 2026 sample ballot to confirm.

Operating referendum (Nov. 3, 2026): the board voted 6-0 in June 2026 to place an operating referendum on the ballot {at_jun19_26}. The state-approved question asks for a rate of up to $0.22 per $100 of assessed value for up to eight years, raising at most $3,606,064 a year, to fund current programs 'in response to reductions in property tax revenue, including student transportation, maintaining class sizes, school safety, and recruiting and retaining staff'; the county-certified cost for a $200,000 median home is $191 a year {dlgf_scs}. Vance said it 'is not intended to expand programs', and the district cited SEA 1 and declining enrollment {at_jun19_26}. The Shelbyville Central Teachers Association endorsed the referendum in September 2026 {at_sep30_26}.

Budget and staffing (2025-2026): in August 2025 Vance said 'our funding is going to be cut significantly', called 2026, 2027 and 2028 'major concerns', and said seven certified positions were left unfilled for financial and enrollment reasons {at_aug17_25}. In December 2025 he listed savings from unfilled positions, fewer bus routes, higher preschool tuition and health insurance changes {at_dec17_25}. In May 2026 Vance and Business Manager Michelle Babcock reported about $1.2 million in savings this year and $1.1 million projected next year, no reduction in force, a 4% cash balance (schools typically aim for 8% to 12%), and a draw on the rainy day fund earlier in the year {at_may20_26}. In June 2026 the board wrote off about $175,000 in uncollectible cafeteria debt {at_jun17_26}.

Academics: 86.2% of SCS third graders (237 of 275) passed IREAD in 2026 {at_aug15_26}. On the 2026 ILEARN, 25% of SCS students in grades 3-8 were proficient in both English and math, below the county rate of 27.6% {at_oct10_26}. In April 2026 Assistant Superintendent Kathleen Miltz briefed the board on the state's new 100-point accountability framework {at_apr23_26}.

Student behavior and safety: in April 2026 teachers association president Teresa Meredith told the board a teacher task force was developing action steps on student behavior for 2026-27; Vance said the district had added behavior support staff, counseling and school resource officer coverage {at_apr23_26}. Vance said in 2025 the district had run a large-scale reunification drill {at_aug17_25}.
Facilities: Vance said in August 2025 that a middle school renovation would start mid-year and take about 18 months, with high school locker room work to follow {at_aug17_25}.

Forums: this guide found no 2026 school board candidate forum or questionnaire. Shelby County Democrats scheduled a 'Local Government 101' civic education session on Oct. 28, 2026, which the organizers said would not focus on individual candidates; Vance is to speak there about the referendum {at_oct10_26}.
Party labels: all three candidates are listed as Nonpartisan on the state list {in_list}.

review_flags.person: David Finkel (former board vice president; not a 2026 candidate)
review_flags.summary: FOX59 reported that FBI agents searched Finkel's Shelbyville home on June 5, 2025 in a federal investigation; the board asked him to resign, calling it 'a personal issue and not conduct involving the school district', and the superintendent confirmed his resignation on June 12, 2025 {fox59_finkel}. The board accepted the resignation and took applications for the vacancy, which it filled with Dr. Julie Ruschhaupt on June 26, 2025 {at_jun13_25}{at_jun27_25}. The article reported no charges and no statement from Finkel {fox59_finkel}.
review_flags.note: Explains how the District 4 seat now held by appointee Ruschhaupt became vacant (seat match inferred from 2022 results, not confirmed). The profile text refers only to a 'vacant seat'. Finkel is not on the 2026 ballot; no charge or outcome confirmed.
